title: Crisp replaced "Give your customer experience a human touch" with an AI-first headline
body: The original H1 **"Give your customer experience a human touch"** positioned the product around warmth and personal service. The new version — **"Augment your customer experience. AI made to support your team & customers."** — leads with AI capability instead. This suggests the team is now targeting buyers who prioritise automation over human interaction, or who already accept AI as table stakes.

title: The new meta description dropped "14 Days free trial. No credit-card required. Try now!" entirely
body: The 2022 meta description used urgency language and multiple CTAs. The current version reads as a category definition: **"Crisp is the ultimate all-in-one AI-powered multichannel messaging platform"**. No trial mention. No exclamation marks. This likely signals a shift away from chasing search-driven trial signups toward attracting buyers who already know they need a platform and are comparing vendors.

title: Crisp added "Build your perfect AI Agent in 4 steps" as a section heading — feature specificity replaced platform breadth
body: The old homepage included section headings like **"Meet the business messaging platform that gathers customer support, sales, and marketing"** — broad capability claims. The new structure foregrounds **"Build your perfect AI Agent in 4 steps"** and **"Let your users search for answers themselves"**. These headings assume the reader already understands what an AI agent is and wants implementation detail, not category education.

title: 6 section headings added and 3 removed points to a structural, not cosmetic, repositioning
body: Crisp did not tweak copy — the team rewrote the homepage architecture. The removed headings focused on **"customer engagement"** and **"all together"** platform messaging. The added headings emphasise AI agents, multichannel inboxes, and self-service knowledge bases. This volume of structural change suggests the company is filtering for a different buyer: someone evaluating AI support tools, not generic SMB messaging platforms.
